intro: A habit uses the indicative; a future event that has not happened yet, after «cuando» or «en cuanto», uses the subjunctive.
p.cuando.consejo: Without an accent it joins two actions. With an accent, «¿cuándo?», it is a question.
p.en cuanto.consejo: It says something happens right away. If it is future, it goes with the subjunctive: «en cuanto llegue».
p.tiempo.consejo: «Tener tiempo» means being free. It also means weather: «hace buen tiempo».
p.llamar.consejo: The ll sounds like y: «ya-MAR». With a pronoun it joins: «llámame».
p.llegar.consejo: Before e it is written «gu»: «llegue», «llegues». That way it keeps the g sound.
p.leer.consejo: «Leo» and «lee» have two strong vowels: they are said in separate syllables: «LE-o», «LE-e».
p.costumbre.consejo: It is feminine: «una costumbre». «Tengo la costumbre de leer» means doing it often.
p.futuro.consejo: The subjunctive with «cuando» speaks of the future, even if the verb looks present.
p.todavía.consejo: The accent marks the «i»: «to-da-BI-a». «Todavía no» means «not yet».
p.escribir.consejo: «Te escribo» can mean «te escribiré» if you speak of the near future.
p.luego.consejo: It is used for the next moment: «luego te cuento». Also: «hasta luego».
b1.titulo: A habit, or something that has not happened yet
b1.texto:
For a situation that **repeats**, use the **indicative**:

- **Cuando tengo** tiempo, leo.

For a **future** action that has not happened yet, use the **subjunctive** after **cuando** or **en cuanto**:

- **Cuando tenga** tiempo, te llamaré.
- **En cuanto llegue**, te escribo.

The other part of the sentence can be in the **future** (te llamaré), in the **present with future meaning** (te escribo) or in the **imperative** (llámame).

If the event already happened, you go back to the indicative: **cuando llegué**, llovía.
b2.f0.texto: When I have time, I read in the park.
b2.f1.texto: When I have time, I will call you.
b2.f2.texto: When are you going to have time?
b2.f3.texto: As soon as I finish work, I will write to you.
b2.f4.texto: Call me when you get home.
b2.f5.texto: Later I will tell you about the trip calmly.
b2.f6.texto: When you arrive, I will prepare dinner.
b2.f7.texto: I always call when I arrive.
b4.texto:
With **cuando** and **en cuanto** choose the mood according to the time:

- **Habit**: indicative. Cuando llego a casa, leo un rato.
- **Past**: indicative. Cuando llegué a casa, llovía.
- **Future** (it has not happened yet): subjunctive. Cuando llegue a casa, leeré un rato.

The main verb can be future, present or imperative: cuando llegues, **llámame**.

A trick: if you can add «todavía no» and the sentence still makes sense, use the subjunctive.
b4.e0.texto: When I get home, I read for a while.
b4.e1.texto: When I get home, I will read for a while.
b4.e2.texto: Call me when you have time.
b5.f0.texto: Every afternoon Lucía opens the window and waits for the sound of the postman.
b5.f1.texto: The street smells of toasted bread and wet leaves.
b5.f2.texto: A sleeping dog wags its tail next to the baker's door.
b5.f3.texto: The bells of the square mark seven with three slow strokes.
b5.f4.texto: The postman turns the corner with his grey bag over his shoulder.
b5.f5.texto: Lucía receives a blue envelope with a small stamp.
b5.f6.texto: Inside there is a letter written in green ink.
b5.f7.texto: Pablo's handwriting hops like a bird between the lines.
b5.f8.texto: Each sentence brings the distant smell of a seaside city.
b5.f9.texto: Lucía folds the paper slowly and keeps it close to her heart.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! A future that has not happened yet: subjunctive.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That is a habit, and it says nothing about a call.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That has already happened: the call was yesterday.
b6.pregunta: The call has not happened yet. Which sentence?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Tengo» is indicative; for a habit yes, for a plan no.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Well done! A future that has not happened yet: subjunctive.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Tuve» is past; here you speak of the future.
b7.pregunta: It is a plan for the future. What is missing?
b8.traduccion: Call me when you get home
b9.o0.refuerzo: That's it! A habit goes with the indicative.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Tenga» is for a future that has not happened.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The future does not go after «cuando».
b9.pregunta: Reading when you have time is a habit. What is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: The subjunctive is for the future that has not happened.
b10.o1.refuerzo: After «cuando» you need a conjugated verb.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Yes! What repeats goes with the indicative.
b10.pregunta: Which mood goes after «cuando» in a habit?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «Call me when you arrive».
b12.frase: En cuanto ____ a casa, te escribo.
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Llego» would be a habit; here it is a near future.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Well done! A future that has not happened: subjunctive (with «gu»).
b12.pregunta: You have not arrived yet. What is missing?
p.llamaré.consejo: From «llamar». The -é ending is the future for «yo»: «I will».
p.llegues.consejo: From «llegar». After «cuando» for the future, use the subjunctive: «llegues».
p.preparo.consejo: From «preparar», to get ready. The ending -o means «I».
p.llego.consejo: From «llegar». The «ll» sounds like «y», and the ending -o means «I».
p.leeré.consejo: From «leer». The -eré ending is the future for «yo».
p.dormido.consejo: From «dormir», to sleep. «Dormido» describes someone who is already asleep.
p.campanas.consejo: Large metal bells that ring in towers. It is feminine plural.
p.marcan.consejo: From «marcar». Here the bells show the time, like a clock does.
p.escrita.consejo: From «escribir». It agrees with «carta», a feminine noun, so it ends in -a.
p.indicativo.consejo: A verb mood used for real facts. The «v» in Spanish sounds like «b».
